_purpose: Which tennis competitions are played best-of-five. Read on both sides of one comparison, through a single loader in src/bet/simple_stats/providers.py: ANALYZE asks what format tonight's fixture is played to, and the ingest side asks whether a historical espn-tennis row was a Grand Slam match (a pinned name is one). scope_values then removes the best-of-three observations from a best-of-five sample -- MATCH_FORMAT_MISMATCH for a match that states a tour draw, MATCH_FORMAT_UNKNOWN for one that states none -- and only when nothing is left does analyze.suppressed_markets_for withhold the length-dependent markets (total_sets, total_games, games_won, aces, double faults, breaks) entirely.
_why: Known and written down in src/bet/simple_stats/contracts.py and src/bet/api_clients/superbet.py since 2026-08-31, still unfixed on 2026-09-01: 'every ATP fixture was quoted best-of-five against a stats sheet that only emits best-of-three lines'. That day the analyst wrote 154 vetoes, 137 of them patching this one hole row by row -- and one leak still reached the operator, because build_coupons applied vetoes to singles and not to Bet Builder legs. Molcan-Bonzi went out as a slip whose legs were 'total_games UNDER 34.5' and 'total_sets UNDER 3.5' at 15/15, off a sample whose maximum was 3.0 sets. Under 3.5 sets in a best-of-three match is not a bet, it is a tautology; Superbet priced the same leg at 2.40 because it was pricing a best-of-five event.
_rule: Exact competition-name pin, matching EventRecord.competition as DISCOVER writes it. Unlisted means unknown, and unknown gates nothing -- the rows are emitted as before. Only BO5 is actionable; BO3 entries are recorded so that a competition which has been checked is distinguishable from one nobody has looked at.
_every_entry_is_a_grand_slam: providers._row_match_level reads 'pinned in this table' as 'Grand Slam draw', which holds because men's Grand Slam main-draw singles is the whole of best-of-five in the professional game and the WTA halves exist only to record that they were checked. Adding a best-of-three tour event here would break that inference; tests/simple_stats/test_tennis_draw_scope.py::test_every_pinned_name_is_a_grand_slam is where it says so.
_what_this_replaced: Until 2026-09-03 the gate had no per-observation draw to read, so it guessed best-of-five from match length: a sample at least a third of which ran to four sets or longer was taken to be best-of-five. That quantity cannot answer the question -- a best-of-five won 3-0 and a best-of-three won 2-1 are both three sets. Measured on the 2026-09-03 ATP US Open slate: 225 of 474 total_sets observations were exactly three and therefore mute, 205 were two-set matches (impossible in best-of-five), all 15 fixtures scored under the threshold, and the entire men's slate came off a 708-row tennis sheet on fully enriched nine-metric dossiers. Only 153 of the slate's 1,530 tennis-abstract observations were Grand Slam matches: 90% of a men's sample is tour tennis, and deleting the market was deleting the 10% along with it.
_scope: Men's Grand Slam main-draw singles is the whole of best-of-five in professional tennis today. Women's draws at the same tournaments are best-of-three, which is why ATP and WTA are separate entries here and must never be folded into one 'US Open'.
